title: Authority grant
description: A human delegating named decisions to a coordinator for a named scope, within limits, until an expiry or a stop condition. Everything not granted stays human-owned (state-machines/authority.yaml). A grant never waives repository policy, protected branches, independent review or required checks.

granted_by.description: The human who holds the authority being delegated: an owner of the grants path (CODEOWNERS), who commits the live grant file (promptbook grant verify --git).

role.description: The coordinator role. Workers never hold a grant; a coordinator passes them only their bounded assignment.

agent.description: An exact agent identity, when the grant is for one session and not the role.

source.description: Where the human said it: a commit, an issue comment, a transcript reference. A worker's claim of delegation is not a source.

actions.description: The decisions delegated. Each is a separate grant: finalize does not imply merge, merge does not imply publish-review.

budget.description: Spend across the grant. Required unless stop_when bounds the grant (grant-is-bounded): a runtime that reports no spend records none it was not told.

stop_when.description: Conditions that end the delegation early (the agreed outcome, repeated non-progress, a consequential ambiguity). A grant that names one may omit expires_at and budget (grant-is-bounded).

expires_at.description: When the grant ends. Required unless limits.stop_when bounds it (grant-is-bounded): no grant is open-ended. Renewing is a new grant from the human, never a saved summary.

revocable.description: Always true: the human may narrow or revoke at any time.

narrowed.description: Narrowing history, append-only and structured: each entry removes actions or scope, or reduces limits or the expiry, of the grant in force. The issued fields stay as issued; the grant in force is them minus every entry (narrowing-only-narrows). Widening is a new grant.

by.description: A human owner of the grants path; a coordinator drafts the narrowing of its own grant and stops exercising it, and the human commits it.

remove_actions.description: Action names to drop (removing merge drops every merge action).

remove_scope.description: Entries to drop from the scope's lists; emptying a list would leave it unrestricted, so it is not a narrowing (revoke instead).

reduce_limits.description: New, lower limits or an earlier expiry; a higher value is widening.

allOf.description: No grant is open-ended: it names an expiry and a budget, or a stop condition (limits.stop_when) that ends it; revocation bounds every grant.
A revocation names who revoked it.
Only a coordinator (orchestrator) or the merge role may hold merge authority.

repo.description: owner/name on the forge, or a host-qualified host/owner/name.

policy.description: How the action is exercised, e.g. for dispose-findings: fix material in-scope findings, defer tangential ones.

mergeAction.description: Merge authority names the repository, the target branch, the repository's protected branch (which the target never is: a grant lands only on a non-protected integration branch, and the protected branch is reached by a human's merge) and the strategy, and still requires the reviewer's pass on the current head and the required checks.

target.description: One exact branch; no wildcard; never protected_branch (merge-target-not-protected).

protected_branch.description: The repository's protected (default) branch as the human states it. The coordinator checks it against the forge before every merge; a target equal to it is invalid.

requires.description: Must include independent-review and required-checks; a merge grant never waives either.
